title: a-proof-cannot-seed-the-tree-it-reads
intention: A proof run cannot write into the live instance tree, so every record standing in ~/.cairn/logs is something that actually happened.
why: MEASURED 2026-08-18, hours after the trail gained its default: 2,080 records stand across 8 device trails in ~/.cairn/logs, and at least 440 of them are FIXTURES — pointers like validation-verdict-changed-test-thing, ground-loop-device-liar, ground-loop-device-broken, invented so a proof could watch a device react to them, re-appended on every `bin/cmd/test` run. They are not in a separate file that could be dropped whole: they are interleaved with real records of identical shape, in the trail whose most frequent pointer (224 hits, ground-loop-is-older-than-the-code-it-judges) IS a real trouble on file in the commons. Nothing marks which is which. THE LIVED SYMPTOM is the one this whole tree exists to remove: a mind arrives at a red, reads the logs for the picture of what just happened, and roughly one record in five describes an event that never occurred — so the surface built to save an exploration funds a wrong one instead. THE DEFECT IN ONE SENTENCE: the seam that isolates a proof's trail EXISTS and is optional — set_diagnostic_roots, proven in test_device_logs_unwired.py, used by 2 proofs of 126 — which is policy standing exactly where physics belongs (Law 4). AND THE REASON IS SPECIFIC, not general sloppiness: every OTHER store in the corpus isolates by construction, because its caller must hand it a root and there is no default to forget (the commons troubles store is clean). The trail is the one store with a default that resolves to the live world, and it grew that default this morning — in the same act that made an unwired device log, which was the right change. A store with a live default is one forgotten line from seeding the instrument it is about to read, which is a failure this corpus has already measured twice (15 of 19 production rows written by their own test). AKIEN'S FRAMING, 2026-08-18: 'so what you're saying is we need a test-fixture space that's not part of the main workspaces' — and his ruling on where it belongs: 'it can still share the parent logging ticket as parent. folding it in would add a more specific into a less specific. less good that.'
traces_to: Law 7 first — a record of truth may never carry an invented record, and 440 of 2,080 describe events that never occurred, in the same files and the same shape as the ones that did. Law 8 — a proof that seeds the tree it later reads is the hollow build by construction. Law 4 — the seam that would fix it exists and is optional, which is policy where physics belongs. Law 3 — the tree is the corpus's record of what was observed, and a fifth of it is fiction.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant, transcribed: PROVED, and feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8). PROVE GATE: the tester runs the proof beside the component it changes — cairn/devices/tester/ — with at least one tooth a hollow build could not pass: a BEFORE/AFTER byte witness over the real ~/.cairn/logs across a proof run that DOES emit, so the tooth reads the world rather than asking the tester whether it isolated. A second non-hollow tooth is required by the prior art: the seal is probed FROM INSIDE the run (the subject asserts its own resolved instance root is not the live one) and an unconfirmable seal is INDETERMINATE, never green — isolation.py's rule, inherited verbatim. DURABILITY GATE: not done until proven AND committed (git). WATCH GATE: WATCHME(a_proof_cannot_seed_the_tree_it_reads), spec in `watchme`, probe armed at the berth it names. PARENT GATE: this is the fourth child of every-boundary-crossing-lands-in-the-logs-tree and proves before that parent crosses PROVED.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when a full `bin/cmd/test` run leaves ~/.cairn/logs byte-identical — asserted by the tester over its own run, the byte-witness shape already carried by bin/proofs/test_delete_gate.py, never a human reading a diff. WRONG INTENT if: the isolation is set but never probed from inside, so a proof that escaped it still reports green (the hollow seal — isolation.py's falsifier clause (5) names exactly this shape one resource over); or it is bought by making every proof remember a call, which is the policy it replaces wearing a new name; or relocating HOME breaks a component that hand-spells an absolute instance path rather than resolving through address.py — in which case the census of those sites is the finding, and it is a better one than the one intended.
falsifier.horizon: the next full corpus run after the seam lands — measurable the same day, needing no clock and no live host. No later than the parent's own crossing, which this gates: the parent measures coverage as trails-on-disk, and that number cannot be read honestly while a fifth of the records in it are staged.

how: HOME IS ALREADY THE DIAL, and finding that is what makes this cheap. address.py computes _INSTANCE = Path.home() / '.cairn' at import, and Path.home() reads $HOME through pathlib — which the floor already imports — so pointing a proof's subprocess at a temp HOME relocates the WHOLE instance root with no change to address.py and no new import. MEASURED BEFORE CASTING (Law 3): a fixture record aimed at the trouble device under a temp HOME landed in the temp world, and the live trail stayed at 292 records. THE OWNER ALREADY EXISTS and it is the tester — cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py already owns what a proof can reach, with a MEASURED network seal — so this extends an existing remit from the network to instance-space rather than minting a mechanism, and it inherits that seal's discipline verbatim: PROBED FROM INSIDE, never assumed, an unconfirmable seal INDETERMINATE rather than green. THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION IS THE WRONG ONE and is recorded here so it is not re-derived: putting the dial inside address.py would satisfy this ticket and break that module's charter bound (it resolves and never touches disk; its single-import floor is a measured claim two other proofs' allowlists admit by name). The environment is the dial instead. Bwrap bind-mounting a temp dir over ~/.cairn is the hardening above the floor, not the floor — it is opt-in per run and absent on some hosts.
